messages:
jaspreet: Quick follow-up from the postmortem — we've seen three recurrent tail-latency spikes on infer-gpu-prod over the last 3 weeks. Need to assign remediation owners, set timelines, and decide whether SLO/SLA tweaks are needed. Thoughts?

maria: I mapped the incidents -> seems correlated with long sequences + cache-thrashing on node pool A. link: https://dash.redwood.internal/d/seq/inf-latency (watch 99p) :point_up:

alex: can we split dashboards by model-size? current aggregated 99p hides smaller-model regressions. I can add a per-model panel + heatmap.

ken: customer impact check — any SLA violations reported? I saw two support tickets but not a formal SLA breach. we should be careful before changing SLA numbers.

sara: Agree with alex; also we should add error-budget burn alerts at 50% and 80% for the 99p window. If burn crosses 80% for a 7d rolling window, trigger an incident and a remediation sprint.

jaspreet: Proposal: 1) Dashboard split by model-size + seq-length buckets (alex) 2) Investigate cache eviction policy on pool A (maria) 3) Temp SLO softening: declare a 30d exploratory buffer to avoid customer-facing SLA changes, monitor impact (ken) 4) Add error-budget alerts (sara). Owners + ETA?

alex: I'll add dashboard panels and a synthetic probe for 95/99/99.9. ETA EOD tomorrow. snippet for probe query I plan to use:

```
avg_over_time(latency_ms{env="prod",model=~"gpt-.*"}[5m])
```

maria: I'll run heap + eviction traces on pool A, and try increasing KV cache size by 20% in a canary. ETA 48h. I'll post logs to the thread.

ken: OK to treat SLO change as 'monitoring-only' for 30d. I'll draft an internal note for sales/support so they can respond to customer questions. ETA COB Friday.

sara: I'll add the error-budget rules and set up a playbook line: if 80% burn -> owner oncall paused from new rollouts + remediation sprint kick. ETA 24h.

jaspreet: Assigning owners: alex (dash+probe), maria (eviction+canary), sara (alerts+playbook), ken (customer comms). I'll track as action items in the postmortem tracker. Targets: dashboards + alerts within 48h, canary + traces within 72h, review call next Tue 10am PT.

alertbot: Incident 2026-03-18: added label recurrent-tail-latency, linked to postmortem PM-4321.

maria: quick note — found repeated GC stalls in trace snippet, might be platform-side. posting trace:

```
2026-03-18T09:12:33Z inf-runner[pid=1234]: GC pause 210ms, kv-evict=1, seq_len=1024
2026-03-18T09:12:34Z inf-runner[pid=1234]: cache-miss counter++
```

jaspreet: Good catch. If GC + eviction together cause 99p blowouts, we should model the combined probability and simulate error-budget impact. Can someone add a small sim? alex?

alex: I can spin up a quick sim using historical traces. Will push results as a gist and add to the review agenda. ETA 36h.

ken: If simulation shows >30% increase in 99p risk under typical seq mixes, we should consider a short-term throttling policy for very long inputs to protect SLA-critical customers. Not a permanent change, just stop-gap.

jaspreet: Noted. Next steps summary (I'll post to the tracker): - Dash split + probe (alex) - Eviction traces + canary (maria) - Alerts + playbook (sara) - Customer comms note (ken) - Simulation + risk numbers (alex) - Review call Tue 10am PT (all).

sara: adding runbook line: "When 7d error budget burn >80%: pause non-critical model rollouts, escalate to eng-sre, open remediation sprint with 3-day SLA to reduce burn."

maria: I'll include the canary's perf baseline and compare 95/99 before/after. If improvement <10% will propose config rollback.

jaspreet: Thanks all. I'll update the postmortem actions and ping owners on Deliverables board. Please update this thread with any blockers. :thumbsup:
